controls.title: Audit controls — hardware, software, and procedural mechanisms that record activity in systems that contain or use ePHI
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That all relevant activity was emitted, that the audit-control mechanism design is appropriate, or that the right activity types were chosen for logging. The chain receives what is emitted to it; coverage is the covered entity's design call.
controls.what_we_prove: Activity events submitted by in-scope systems containing or using ePHI are recorded with tamper-evident ordering, signed timestamps, and cryptographic anchoring. An auditor or OCR investigator can verify the recorded activity has not been altered since logging.

controls.title: Integrity — protect ePHI from improper alteration or destruction (audit-log integrity only)
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That ePHI in primary storage was protected from alteration. The chain attests integrity OF the audit log; protecting the underlying ePHI is the covered entity's responsibility outside the chain.
controls.what_we_prove: The chain itself is integrity-protected: hash-linking + signature anchoring make any after-the-fact alteration of recorded events detectable. For events that include ePHI integrity-check results, the chain preserves the result with tamper-evident ordering.

controls.title: Information system activity review
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the review was substantive, that the right activities were reviewed, or that follow-up actions were adequate. The chain records the review; the policy and rigor of the review are the covered entity's call.
controls.what_we_prove: Records of information-system-activity review events (who reviewed what, when, what action they took) submitted to the chain are stored with tamper-evident ordering. An auditor can verify the review actually happened on the date claimed.

controls.title: Log-in monitoring
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the monitoring detects anomalies, that failed log-ins trigger appropriate response, or that the authentication system itself is correctly designed.
controls.what_we_prove: Log-in events (successful and failed) submitted to the chain are stored with stable cryptographic ordering and signed timestamps. An auditor can reconstruct authentication patterns over the retention period.

controls_out_of_scope.reason: security management process design is administrative/organizational
assigned security responsibility is an organizational role assignment
workforce security (authorization, supervision, termination) is HR/process-level
information access management (authorization policy) is process-level
security awareness and training (except log-in monitoring above) is organizational
security incident procedures are workflow-level (specific incidents may be logged elsewhere)
contingency plan and data backup are operational design
periodic security evaluation is a process, not chain-evidenced
physical safeguards (facility access, workstation use, device controls) are out of scope for a cryptographic audit chain
unique user identification is an identity-system property; the chain records the identifier in events but does not enforce uniqueness
emergency access procedure design is operational, not chain-evidenced
automatic logoff is an authentication-system feature, not chain-evidenced
encryption and decryption of ePHI at rest is system-level, not chain-evidenced
person or entity authentication is an identity-system property
transmission security is a transport-layer concern (encryption in transit, integrity controls); specific transmission events may be logged
Business Associate Agreement requirements are contractual
policies, procedures, and documentation are document-level
